I still couldn't install gbrain, and I've stopped there. Hermes's security scanner blocked the same command again:

  bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#v0.60.757.0

Its offline package checks can't finish. This session has no one to approve, so any command that fails those checks is blocked. "Carry on without me" isn't approval to get around the scanner. I won't install from my local clone, use another package manager, or change the scanner settings myself.

The free, no-API-key setup you asked for is what the docs give by default. Install just the gbrain command-line tool locally, skip hosted gbrain.io, and search works by keyword until you add a key. Nothing else to decide.

Bun 1.4.5 is installed in ~/.bun/bin. Either way below works:

1. Run it yourself:
     export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH"
     bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#v0.60.757.0
     gbrain --version

2. Tell me directly that I may change the Hermes approval setting (approvals.single_query_mode: approve in config.yaml), or run me in an interactive session where you can approve the command. I'll then install it, check the version, and complete the free setup.
